svg.title: Forces overview
svg.desc: Vectors & resultants: Vectors have magnitude + direction; scalars have magnitude only. Force in N; weight W = mg. Resultant combines forces. Zero resultant → constant velocity, possibly zero. Resolve perpendicular components with scale drawings. Work & springs: W = Fs; F = ke; Eₑ = ½ke². Use extension in m. Spring equations within proportional limit. Elastic returns to original shape; inelastic leaves deformation. Measure force/extension with ruler and known loads. Moments & pressure: M = Fd, perpendicular d. Balance clockwise/anticlockwise moments. Levers/gears transmit turning. p = F/A; p = hρg. Greater depth → greater p; pressure difference gives upthrust. Motion & laws: v = s/t; a = Δv/t; v²−u² = 2as for constant acceleration. Distance–time slope = speed; velocity–time slope = a, area = displacement. F = ma; third-law forces act on different objects. Stopping & falling: Stopping = thinking + braking. Thinking = vt; braking transfers kinetic energy to thermal stores. Weight > drag → accelerates. Drag grows with speed until forces balance at terminal velocity. Momentum: p = mv; F = Δp/Δt. Closed system: total momentum conserved. Use signed velocities. Airbags/mats increase stopping time, reducing average force for the same momentum change.
